data.title: Bursa Malaysia Ends Week Lower As FBM KLCI Slips 3.37 Points Amid Weak Buying Interest
data.description:
Bursa Malaysia closed lower on Nov 13, with the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) shedding 3.37 points or 0.21% to 1,582.59, as weak buying interest and persistent investor caution weighed on the local market.

At 5pm, the benchmark index had eased from its close of 1,585.96 on Nov 12, after fluctuating between 1,579.66 and 1,588.10 during the trading session.

The broader market suffered steeper losses, with the FBM 70 tumbling 165.24 points or 0.97% to 16,783.33.

The F4GBM declined 4.16 points or 0.44% to 951.19, while the FBM Emas fell 51.20 points or 0.43% to 11,736.89.

The FBM Shariah also recorded substantial losses, sliding 93.59 points or 0.79% to 11,679.68.

MMAG Holdings Bhd dominated trading activity, with 233.07 million shares changing hands, although its share price dropped one sen to three sen.

Zetrix AI Bhd followed with 115.24 million shares traded, gaining half a sen to six sen, while CBH Engineering Holding Bhd plunged 14 sen to 68 sen on 99.35 million shares.

Nexgram Holdings Bhd remained unchanged at 5.5 sen, with 83.5 million shares traded.

GIIB Holdings Bhd rounded out the five most active counters, surging 2.5 sen to 13 sen on 56.02 million shares.

The weak closing performance reflected a lack of sustained buying momentum, with selling pressure extending beyond heavyweight stocks into the broader market as investors remained cautious heading into the weekend.

data.title: Nestlé, MPI Lead Bursa Losers As Selling Pressure Outweighs Gains
data.description:
Nestlé (M) Bhd and Malaysian Pacific Industries Bhd (MPI) led the stock market’s top losers on Nov 13, as selling pressure persisted across the broader market, with decliners significantly outnumbering gainers.

Market breadth remained negative, with 686 losers against 369 gainers, while 497 counters were unchanged, 1,232 untraded and 16 suspended.

Nestlé emerged as the biggest loser, plunging RM1.94 to RM93, followed by MPI, which tumbled RM1.32 to RM37.20.

ViTrox Corporation Bhd shed 60 sen to RM9.50, while Kuala Lumpur Kepong Bhd declined 52 sen to RM20.86. Mi Technovation Bhd rounded out the top five losers, dropping 50 sen to RM5.75.

On the upside, Mega Fortris Bhd emerged as the top gainer, surging 23 sen to RM1.24, followed by RHB Bank Bhd, which climbed 20 sen to RM7.73.

Sarawak Oil Palms Bhd advanced 17 sen to RM5.48, while Hengyuan Refining Company Bhd gained 15 sen to RM2.75.

Master-Pack Group Bhd completed the top five gainers, rising 12 sen to RM1.54.

Despite selective buying interest, overall trading activity moderated as investors remained cautious.

Total turnover fell to 2.84 billion shares worth RM2.36 billion compared to previous day’s turnover of 3.06 billion shares valued at RM2.56 billion.

The weaker market breadth and declining turnover reflected subdued investor sentiment, with selling pressure dominating trading despite gains in selected banking, plantation and industrial counters.

data.title: Stock Today: Hartalega Dips 1.89% Despite 83% Jump In Quarterly Net Profit
data.description:
Hartalega Holdings Bhd shares fell 2 sen or 1.89% to RM1.04 as at 2.53pm, following Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB)’s downgrade of the glove manufacturer to Sell from Hold.

The counter opened at RM1.07 before reaching an intraday high of RM1.09 and a low of RM1.02, with 6.82 million shares traded.

At the time of writing, the buying queue stood at RM1.03 with 546,900 shares, while the selling queue was at RM1.04 with 116,300 shares.

HLIB lowered its target price for Hartalega to RM0.80 from RM0.97, citing persistent industry oversupply, weaker crude oil prices and rising operating costs that could weigh on earnings.

The research house warned that third-quarter earnings could remain broadly flat despite management’s expectation of a 10% quarter-on-quarter recovery in sales volume, as weaker average selling prices and higher natural gas expenses could offset potential improvements in inventory costs.

The downgrade came despite Hartalega reporting an 83.3% year-on-year increase in second-quarter net profit to RM32.8 million, supported by higher average selling prices, improved production efficiency and tighter cost controls.

Revenue for the quarter ended Sept 30, 2026 rose 19.5% to RM644.7 million from RM539.7 million a year earlier.

For the first half of FY2027, operating profit surged 461.6% to RM120.4 million, with its operating profit margin widening to 9.6% from 2% previously.

However, HLIB maintained that structural oversupply, energy costs and wage pressures would continue to constrain the industry’s recovery, arguing that recent gains in Malaysian glove stocks were not fully supported by underlying fundamentals.

data.title: Bursa Malaysia Slips At Midday Amid Regional Weakness
data.description:

The FBM Emas slipped 25.02 points or 0.21% to 11,763.07, while the FBM Shariah declined 31.48 points or 0.27% to 11,741.79.

Market breadth remained negative, with 541 losers outnumbering 294 gainers. A total of 468 counters were unchanged, 2,784 untraded and 16 suspended.

UMS Integration Ltd led the decliners, falling 34 sen to RM6.86, followed by Sunway Construction Group Bhd, which dropped 33 sen to RM7.74.

Allianz Malaysia Bhd slipped 30 sen to RM19.16, while Dutch Lady Milk Industries Bhd and Kuala Lumpur Kepong Bhd each declined 22 sen to RM28.28 and RM21.16, respectively.

Meanwhile, PIE Industrial Bhd emerged as the top gainer, rising 18 sen to RM1.68.

Carlsberg Brewery Malaysia Bhd and United Plantations Bhd each gained 16 sen to RM13.26 and RM31.76, respectively, while Sarawak Oil Palms Bhd climbed 14 sen to RM5.45.

Hengyuan Refining Company Bhd rounded out the top five gainers, advancing 13 sen to RM2.73.

Meanwhile, MMAG Holdings Bhd topped the most actively traded list with 163.89 million shares changing hands, slipping half a sen to 3.5 sen.

CBH Engineering Holdings Bhd followed with 72.21 million shares traded, declining 14 sen to 68 sen, while Zetrix AI Bhd remained unchanged at 5.5 sen on 52.57 million shares.

VS Industry Bhd eased one sen to 27.5 sen, with 34.03 million shares traded, while Nexgram Holdings Bhd remained flat at 5.5 sen on 34 million shares.

Total trading volume for midday stood at 1.59 billion units valued at RM948.03 million.

The subdued midday performance reflected continued investor caution, with selling pressure across key indices outweighing selective buying interest in individual counters.

data.title: Gold Sees Sharp Drop, RHB Says It May Decline To US$3,800 Levels
data.description:
RHB Research has shifted to a bearish outlook on COMEX Gold futures, recommending traders initiate short positions after the precious metal suffered a sharp decline that breached its key support level of US$3,900.

In its latest technical analysis report, the research house said gold futures plunged US$115.20 on Thursday to close at US$3,885.30, triggering its previous stop-loss level and signalling a shift in market momentum.

The commodity opened at US$3,994 and briefly climbed to an intraday high of US$4,005.90 before aggressive selling pressure pushed prices to a session low of US$3,856.70.

The session ended with a long bearish candlestick, reflecting strong selling momentum and a decisive break below the US$3,900 support level.

RHB said the technical breakdown indicated that sellers had gained control of the market, raising the likelihood of further downside in the near term.

The precious metal is now trading below both its 20-day and 50-day simple moving averages (SMA), while the Relative Strength Index (RSI) continues to decline towards oversold territory.

These indicators suggest that bearish momentum is strengthening, with limited signs of an immediate recovery.

“In a bearish setup, support levels tend to be weak. Hence, the commodity may extend its decline towards the US$3,800 support,” RHB said.

Following the breach of its previous stop-loss threshold, RHB has closed the long position initiated at US$4,113.50 on November 5.

The research house now recommends traders establish short positions at US$3,885.30, based on the closing price on November 12, with a new stop-loss level set at US$4,100 to manage trading risks.

RHB identified immediate support at US$3,800, followed by a lower support level of US$3,600 should selling pressure intensify.

On the upside, the first resistance is seen at US$4,000, followed by a stronger resistance level at US$4,100.

The research house maintained that gold futures are likely to remain under pressure as long as prices stay below the US$4,100 resistance level.

It reiterated its negative trading bias, citing the breakdown below key technical support levels and weakening momentum indicators as signals of potential further declines in the precious metal.

data.title: Stock Today: Pharmaniaga Climbs 4.67% After Third-Quarter Profit Reaches RM26.9 Million
data.description:
Pharmaniaga Bhd shares rose 4.67% to RM0.785 as at 11.48am, following the group’s announcement of a more than threefold increase in third-quarter profit and stronger earnings for the nine months ended Sept 30, 2026.

The healthcare counter gained 3.5 sen from its last traded price of RM0.75, after opening at RM0.77. It touched an intraday high of RM0.79 and a low of RM0.755, with 2.38 million shares changing hands.

At the time of writing, the buying queue stood at RM0.78 with 15,300 shares, while the selling queue was at RM0.785 with 14,900 shares.

Pharmaniaga reported third-quarter profit after taxation and zakat of RM26.9 million, up from RM7.5 million a year earlier, while revenue increased 0.7% to RM1.01 billion, mainly driven by higher insulin sales.

For the nine-month period, profit after taxation and zakat rose 72% to RM72.2 million from RM42 million, while revenue grew 8.2% to RM3.23 billion on stronger demand in its concession segment.

The group also declared a third interim dividend of 0.32 sen per share for FY2026, with an entitlement date of Dec 24, 2026 and payment scheduled for Jan 20, 2027.

data.title: Stock Today: Johor Plantations Stays Flat After 9M26 Profit Decline
data.description:
Johor Plantations Group Bhd (JPG) shares were unchanged at RM1.80 as at 11.21am, following the group’s report of a 21.3% year-on-year decline in profit after tax (PAT) for the nine months ended Sept 30, 2026.

The plantation counter opened at RM1.80 and traded between RM1.78 and RM1.81, with 701,700 shares changing hands.

At the time of writing, the stock was quoted at RM1.79 on the buying queue and RM1.80 on the selling queue. There were 1,300 shares queued to buy against 269,000 shares offered for sale.

JPG reported 9M26 PAT of RM201.9 million, down from RM256.4 million a year earlier, while revenue edged lower to RM1.22 billion from RM1.23 billion. Internal fresh fruit bunch (FFB) production also fell 11.8% to 712,829 metric tonnes.

The weaker nine-month performance came despite a recovery in the third quarter, when PAT rose 95.6% quarter-on-quarter to RM100.3 million, supported by improved crop production and favourable crude palm oil selling prices.

However, third-quarter PAT remained 5.2% lower year-on-year, while revenue declined 9.2% to RM450.7 million.

The group declared a third interim dividend of 1.5 sen per share for FY26.

data.title: Kospi Jumps 2.35% As Asian Markets Recover From Nvidia-Led Sell-Off
data.description:
Asian stocks recovered on Friday after a turbulent week of trading, although uncertainty surrounding Nvidia’s leadership change continued to raise questions over the outlook for the artificial intelligence industry and its wider supply chain.

MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan rose 0.26%, recovering some of the 1.3% loss recorded in the previous session. South Korea’s Kospi gained 2.35%, while Japan’s Nikkei advanced 1.4%.

The rebound came after Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang resigned on Thursday following reports of extramarital affairs, including one involving a suspected Chinese spy. His departure has raised concerns over the chipmaker’s future direction, particularly its efforts to maintain access to the Chinese market and its role in the global AI infrastructure buildout.

Analysts at JPMorgan said Huang’s exit could leave a leadership gap that would be difficult to fill, while new agreements could take longer or require greater compensation as investors seek reassurance over Nvidia’s role.

They also pointed to potential implications for GPU financing and infrastructure deals involving Nvidia as a supplier, investor or provider of contractual support.

Nvidia shares fell 3% in extended trading, while South Korean internet company Naver, one of its customers, dropped 2.75% on Friday.

However, the uncertainty could benefit rivals including Advanced Micro Devices, Arista Networks and Broadcom, according to Citi’s head of specialist sales and technology, media and telecommunications specialist Jon Zauderer.

“If you think about the uncertainty that’s created about a potential management change, investors are going to look for alternatives,” he said.

The concerns have also extended beyond equities, with London copper prices hitting a four-month low in the previous session amid fears of weaker demand from the AI sector. Shares of Australian-listed miner Capstone Copper fell more than 5% on Friday.

Meanwhile, US Treasury yields climbed as investors increased bets on a larger Federal Reserve rate hike next month, lifting the dollar and putting the yen under pressure.

The two-year US Treasury yield reached 4.8920% in early Asian trading, its highest in a month, while the 10-year yield rose to a three-week high of 5.1433%.

Markets are now pricing in a 14.5% chance of a 50-basis-point Fed rate increase in December, compared with zero a week ago, according to the CME FedWatch tool.

Capital Group fixed income investment director Manusha Samaraweera said further hotter-than-expected inflation readings could leave room for additional rate increases.

The dollar was on track for a weekly gain of 0.9%, its largest in more than a month, while the yen remained near the key 160-per-dollar level, keeping traders alert to possible intervention by Japanese authorities.

Elsewhere, Brent crude futures fell more than 0.3% to US$95.45 a barrel, while US crude declined by a similar margin to US$88.39. Both benchmarks had risen in the previous session following attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure and continued shipping disruptions through the Strait of Hormuz.

Spot gold rose 0.3% to US$3,888.01 an ounce.

Reuters

data.title: Fed Rate Bets Lift Dollar While Yen Struggles To Stay Above 160
data.description:
The US dollar held near a 19-month high on Friday after a sharp rise in Treasury yields and growing expectations of a larger Federal Reserve interest rate increase next month, putting the Japanese yen under renewed pressure near the 160-per-dollar level.

The yen was last little changed at 159.875 per dollar, after briefly touching 160 on Thursday. The level has heightened concerns over possible intervention by Japanese authorities to support the currency.

Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama said on Friday that the government would respond appropriately to currency volatility.

The dollar’s strength followed a 34-basis-point rise in two-year US Treasury yields over the past two sessions, marking their sharpest two-day increase in three-and-a-half years. Yields climbed after US President Donald Trump said Washington did not need a deal with Iran, while investors reassessed the possibility of a larger Fed rate increase in December.

Some Fed officials have warned this week that US inflation remains stubbornly high, with some indicating they would consider a 50-basis-point increase if price pressures fail to ease.

Markets are now pricing in a 14.5% chance of such a move next month, compared with no expectation of a larger hike a week ago, according to the CME FedWatch tool.

The dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies, was last down 0.05% at 103.17, remaining near its highest level since April 2025.

The euro fell 0.1% to US$1.1049, close to its weakest level against the dollar since April 2025. It was down 0.8% for the week and on track for its largest weekly decline since late September.

Commonwealth Bank of Australia currency strategist Carol Kong said a further sharp sell-off in equity markets could weigh on the US dollar, although its recent momentum could continue in the near term if Fed officials provide further support for a larger rate increase.

Investors are also monitoring volatility in technology stocks following Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang’s departure, alongside concerns over funding and regulatory pressures in the sector.

Elsewhere, the Australian dollar has fallen about 2.5% over the past month, making it the weakest-performing Group of 10 currency against the US dollar during that period. It was last trading at US$0.68.

The US dollar was largely steady against the Swiss franc at 0.835, near a one-month high.

Reuters

data.title: Bitcoin Sinks Below US$71,000, Ethereum Hovers Near US$2,000 Amid Heavy Selling
data.description:
The cryptocurrency market suffered another sharp setback on Nov 13, as Bitcoin slipped below US$71,000 and Ethereum approached the US$2,000 mark, with both digital assets hitting their weakest levels since August.

Bitcoin traded at approximately US$70,834, down 3.79% over 24 hours and 6.53% over the past week. Ethereum declined 2.1% to US$2,007.04, taking its weekly losses to 10.11%.

The sustained downturn coincided with growing uncertainty over US monetary policy, as stronger-than-expected inflation figures fuelled expectations of a Federal Reserve interest rate increase in December.

Investor sentiment was further undermined by persistent withdrawals from US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds, which recorded approximately US$1.44 billion in outflows across five trading sessions.

The market turbulence also sparked a wave of forced liquidations, wiping out around US$680.8 million in leveraged cryptocurrency positions within 24 hours. Of that amount, nearly US$599 million involved traders betting on price increases.

Bitcoin-related positions accounted for US$325.3 million in liquidations compared to US$106.1 million for Ethereum, highlighting the scale of the market’s volatility.

Meanwhile, the overall cryptocurrency market lost 5.09% of its value, bringing total market capitalisation to approximately US$2.42 trillion.

Attention now turns to the latest US producer price inflation figures for further clues on interest rate movements, while traders monitor whether Bitcoin can defend the US$70,000 threshold and Ethereum can maintain support around US$2,000 amid the risk of further declines.

data.title: Technology Counters Buck Bursa Weakness, PIE Industrial Leads Early Gainers
data.description:
Bursa Malaysia opened lower on Friday, tracking overnight losses on Wall Street, although buying interest in selected technology stocks helped limit the decline.

The benchmark FBM KLCI slipped 1.41 points or 0.09% to 1,584.55 at 9.16am, after opening 0.47 points lower at 1,585.49.

Overnight, US stocks ended in negative territory after Nvidia’s decline following chief executive Jensen Huang’s departure outweighed gains in energy counters. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 0.36% to 52,297.09, while the S&P 500 shed 0.35% to 7,592.40 and the Nasdaq Composite declined 0.39% to 25,366.09.

On the local bourse, technology-related stocks featured among the early gainers, with PIE Industrial rising 14 sen to RM1.64, UWC gaining 11 sen to RM6.48 and ViTrox adding eight sen to RM10.18.

Master-Pack Group advanced 13 sen to RM1.55, while Mega Fortris climbed eight sen to RM1.09.

Among the decliners, Heineken Malaysia fell 30 sen to RM13.58, Kuala Lumpur Kepong shed 14 sen to RM21.24, PJBumi lost 13 sen to RM4.12 and Mentiga declined nine sen to RM1.06.

Malacca Securities expects the local market to remain under pressure following Wall Street’s overnight performance, although it sees potential buying interest in brewery stocks ahead of year-end festivities and Chinese New Year, when seasonal beer demand could strengthen.

The brokerage also highlighted plantation stocks including Kuala Lumpur Kepong, SD Guthrie and Johor Plantations Group as potential trading opportunities following a rebound in crude palm oil prices.

It favoured 5E Resources following the commissioning of its new Pasir Gudang facility, which has lifted its annual treatment and recycling capacity from 282,000 tonnes to more than 500,000 tonnes.

Meanwhile, Berjaya Research expects sentiment towards the FBM KLCI to remain cautious as investors assess weakness in heavyweight stocks.

The research house said attention would turn to Malaysia’s upcoming retail sales data for indications of domestic consumption strength, alongside US producer price index figures for further clues on inflation and the Federal Reserve’s policy outlook.

It added that the local market was approaching oversold territory, potentially creating opportunities for bargain hunting.

“The immediate resistances are located at 1,600-1,616 points. Meanwhile, the immediate supports are now shifted to 1,580 points, followed by 1,576 points,” Berjaya Research said.

The brokerage expects intermittent profit-taking across the broader market, although rotational interest in selected small- and mid-cap stocks could keep trading activity relatively active.

data.title: Stronger Dollar And Rising Oil Prices Shape Ringgit’s Friday Opening
data.description:
The ringgit opened weaker against the US dollar on Friday but strengthened against most other major currencies, as expectations of a possible US Federal Reserve (Fed) interest rate hike in December continued to support the greenback.

At 8am, the local currency traded at 4.0780/0840 against the US dollar, compared with Thursday’s close of 4.0765/0805.

Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the US Dollar Index continued to climb, reaching 103.198 points, amid expectations that the Fed could tighten monetary policy at its meeting next month.

He noted that Brent crude oil prices had also risen 3.27% to US$95.79 a barrel, suggesting inflationary pressures could remain elevated.

“However, the increase in initial jobless claims to 200,000 last week and a 5.5 per cent month-on-month contraction in existing home sales in the US were largely overlooked by traders, as expectations of a Fed rate hike continued to dominate market sentiment.

“Against this backdrop, the ringgit is expected to trade between RM4.07 and RM4.08 against the US dollar today,” he told Bernama.

Against other major currencies, the ringgit strengthened to 4.5054/5120 against the euro from 4.5225/5269 at Thursday’s close, while rising to 5.3952/4031 against the British pound from 5.4103/4156.

It also appreciated against the Japanese yen to 2.5503/5543 from 2.5524/5551 previously.

Among ASEAN currencies, the ringgit strengthened against the Singapore dollar to 3.1684/1733 from 3.1726/1760 and gained against the Thai baht to 12.0348/0629 from 12.0678/0836.

However, it was little changed against the Indonesian rupiah at 223.5/224.0 compared with 223.5/223.8 previously, while remaining flat against the Philippine peso at 6.40/6.41.

data.title: Singapore Shares Open Lower After Wall Street Retreats On Nvidia Sell-Off
data.description:
Singapore shares opened lower on Friday, tracking overnight losses on Wall Street as concerns surrounding Nvidia’s leadership transition and the outlook for US interest rates weighed on investor sentiment.

The benchmark Straits Times Index (STI) fell 17.10 points or 0.32% to 5,265.60 as at 9.07am.

US stocks ended lower on Thursday, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average declining 0.36% to 52,297.09, the S&P 500 losing 0.35% to 7,592.40 and the Nasdaq Composite slipping 0.39% to 25,366.09.

Nvidia shares fell 4.3% following chief executive Jensen Huang’s departure, although the stock recovered from an earlier decline of nearly 12%. The company’s chief financial officer Colette Kress has been named interim CEO.

The sell-off also weighed on other artificial intelligence-linked stocks, with data centre firms Nebius, CoreWeave, IREN and Applied Digital recording losses. However, Nvidia competitors Broadcom, Advanced Micro Devices and Alphabet moved higher.

Investors were also assessing the Federal Reserve’s interest rate outlook ahead of Friday’s US producer price index release, following hotter-than-expected consumer inflation data earlier in the week. Markets were pricing in at least a 25-basis-point rate hike in December.

Back in Singapore, market breadth was relatively balanced, with 91 counters advancing against 87 decliners. Total trading volume stood at 61.04 million securities, valued at S$128.43 million.

Among the STI constituents, DBS Group Holdings fell S$0.68 or 0.96% to S$70.32, while Singtel traded at S$4.21. Genting Singapore stood at S$0.585.

AEM Holdings was at S$7.22, OCBC Bank at S$28.65, ST Engineering at S$9.56 and Singapore Exchange at S$20.83.

In the real estate investment trust segment, CapitaLand Ascendas REIT was unchanged at S$2.21. Mapletree Logistics Trust traded at S$1.09, CapitaLand Integrated Commercial Trust at S$2.33 and Mapletree Industrial Trust at S$1.72.

Frasers Centrepoint Trust stood at S$2.14, while Keppel DC REIT traded at S$2.16 and United Industrial REIT at S$0.765.

data.title: Stock Picks: CTOS Digital And Sarawak Oil Palms
data.description:
RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) has identified potential upside in CTOS Digital Bhd and Sarawak Oil Palms Bhd, with both stocks showing signs of improving technical momentum following recent rebounds.

In its technical analysis, RHB Research said CTOS Digital could be heading towards a bullish breakout after recovering from its recent low and consolidating sideways. The stock is now trading above its 21-day simple moving average (SMA), suggesting that selling pressure has eased.

However, a close above the RM0.45 resistance is needed to confirm the bullish setup. If the breakout materialises, the stock could advance towards RM0.48, followed by RM0.51.

On the downside, a breach of the RM0.42 support level could weaken market sentiment and expose the stock to a correction.

Meanwhile, Sarawak Oil Palms has already broken above its RM5.30 resistance after rebounding from a two-month low, with RHB Research noting that the stock formed a bullish candlestick in the previous trading session.

The latest price action has also lifted the stock above its 21-day SMA, pointing to an improving near-term trend and a possible reacceleration in bullish momentum.

Following the breakout, Sarawak Oil Palms could test RM5.60 before advancing towards RM5.90. However, a decline below the RM5.00 support would invalidate the bullish outlook and potentially trigger a correction.

data.title: HSIF Tests Bullish Resolve After Losing 50-Day Average
data.description:
The Hang Seng Index Futures (HSIF) fell below the 24,000-point support level on Thursday, extending its losses for a second consecutive session, although RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) maintained its long position call with a stop-loss level at 23,600 points.

The futures contract dropped 294 points to close at 23,984 points after opening at 24,277 points and reaching an intraday high of 24,306 points. Selling pressure subsequently pushed the index to a low of 23,940 points.

In evening trading, the HSIF shed another 70 points to last trade at 23,914 points.

RHB Research said the bearish candlestick formation indicated that selling pressure remained active, with the index slipping below its 50-day simple moving average (SMA). Its Relative Strength Index (RSI) had also eased to the 50% level, pointing to fading bullish momentum.

However, the futures contract remained above its 20-day SMA, which could provide some support in the near term.

The research house said the HSIF could test the 23,600-point support level, but maintained a positive trading bias as long as the index stayed above its 23,600-point stop-loss threshold.

Traders were advised to hold the long position initiated at the Nov 5 closing level of 24,886 points.

Following the breach of 24,000 points, RHB Research placed immediate support at 23,600 points, followed by a lower support at 23,000 points. Resistance levels are pegged at 24,500 points and 25,000 points.

data.title: US Stocks Retreat As Huang Exit Weighs On Nvidia And AI Shares
data.description:
US stocks ended lower on Thursday as losses in Nvidia shares following the resignation of chief executive Jensen Huang outweighed gains in energy stocks, while investors continued to assess the fallout for the artificial intelligence sector and the prospect of higher US interest rates.

Nvidia shares fell 4.3%, recovering from a sharper decline of nearly 12% earlier in the session. Retail investors bought about US$111 million worth of the chipmaker’s shares in the first 30 minutes of trading, marking the largest opening buying spree for the stock, according to Vanda Analytics data.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 189.40 points, or 0.36%, to 52,297.09, while the S&P 500 lost 26.98 points, or 0.35%, to 7,592.40. The Nasdaq Composite declined 100.10 points, or 0.39%, to 25,366.09.

The sell-off in AI-related counters extended beyond Nvidia, with AI cloud firm Nebius tumbling 16.8% after reporting its quarterly results and outlook. CoreWeave dropped 6.9%, while data centre-related firms IREN and Applied Digital fell 6.5% and 5.4%, respectively.

The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index also slipped 0.5%, following a 17.2% rally over the previous four trading sessions.

However, Nvidia’s competitors Broadcom, Advanced Micro Devices and Alphabet moved higher, providing some of the biggest boosts to the S&P 500.

Energy stocks offered some support to the broader market, with the S&P 500 energy sector rising 1.5% for its fourth consecutive session of gains. Crude prices climbed after US President Donald Trump said on social media that Washington did not need a deal with Iran.

Market volatility has increased in recent days amid concerns over potential AI regulation following Democratic victories in the US midterm elections, alongside uncertainty surrounding Nvidia’s leadership transition. The company has appointed chief financial officer Colette Kress as interim CEO following Huang’s departure.

“Right now, the market is selling AI stocks and tech stocks and buying safe stuff, just like it did in the first halo trade in January and February of this year, but it will flip back,” said Jed Ellerbroek, portfolio manager at Argent Capital Management in St Louis.

“That’s the tug of war the market is doing right now. It’s concerns about deceleration versus just pointing out that the absolute valuation and growth rates are still pretty compelling.”

Beyond the leadership uncertainty, investors are also examining Nvidia’s financing arrangements with companies across the AI ecosystem, including some of its own customers.

Ellerbroek described Nvidia as the “circular-funder-in-chief”, adding that he expected such activity to moderate following Huang’s departure.

Investors are also awaiting Friday’s US Producer Price Index data, following a hotter-than-expected consumer inflation reading earlier this week.

Markets are fully pricing in at least a 25-basis-point Federal Reserve rate hike in December, with a 15% probability of a 50-basis-point increase, according to CME FedWatch.

Recent comments from Fed officials have pointed to differing views on the policy outlook. Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack said she did not believe the central bank needed to move towards more aggressive rate increases, while San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly said further hikes would likely be needed to address elevated inflation, although she did not indicate any urgency.

Declining stocks outnumbered advancing issues by a 3.4-to-1 ratio on the New York Stock Exchange and 3.18-to-1 on the Nasdaq.

The S&P 500 recorded 18 new 52-week highs and two new lows, while the Nasdaq Composite registered 55 new highs and 267 new lows. Trading volume across US exchanges reached 19.18 billion shares, above the 20-day average of 18.61 billion shares.

data.title: Losers Outnumber Gainers By More Than Two-To-One As Selling Pressure Persists
data.description:
The stock market remained under selling pressure on Nov 12, with declining stocks outnumbering gainers by more than two-to-one as investors continued to trim their holdings across the broader market.

Market breadth was firmly negative, with 799 losers against just 318 gainers, while 476 counters were unchanged, 1,181 untraded and 13 suspended.

Among the top losers, Nestlé (M) Bhd led the decline, shedding 60 sen to RM94.94, followed by Fraser & Neave Holdings Bhd and Hong Leong Industries Bhd, which both fell 40 sen to RM20.14 and RM16.40, respectively.

YTL Power International Bhd slipped 39 sen to RM4.40, while UWC Bhd declined 31 sen to RM6.37.

On the upside, United Plantations Bhd emerged as the biggest gainer, surging RM1.36 to RM31.60, followed by Heineken Malaysia Bhd, which climbed 56 sen to RM13.88.

Kuala Lumpur Kepong Bhd added 30 sen to RM21.38, while Carlsberg Brewery Malaysia Bhd advanced 26 sen to RM13.10 and Concrete Engineering Products Bhd rose 22 sen to RM4.60.

Despite the weak market sentiment, trading activity increased, with total turnover rising to 3.06 billion shares worth RM2.56 billion compared to 2.9 billion shares valued at RM2.33 billion on Nov 11.

data.title: Bursa Malaysia Falls For Fourth Straight Session, FBM KLCI Slips Below 1,600
data.description:
Bursa Malaysia extended its losing streak to a fourth consecutive session on Nov 12, with the benchmark index slipping further below the 1,600-point level amid persistent broad-based selling pressure.

At 5pm, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) fell 9.23 points, or 0.58%, to 1,585.96 from its close of 1,595.19 on Nov 11.

The benchmark index traded between 1,583.66 and 1,592.89 throughout the session.

The broader market also weakened, with the FBM 70 shedding 169.30 points, or 0.99%, to 16,948.57, while the FBM Emas declined 89.69 points, or 0.76%, to 11,788.09.

The FBM Shariah dropped 98.18 points, or 0.83%, to 11,773.27, while the F4GBM eased 6.93 points, or 0.72%, to 955.35.

Among the most actively traded counters, MMAG Holdings Bhd and Zetrix AI Bhd were unchanged at four sen and 5.5 sen, respectively, with 370.88 million and 65.5 million shares changing hands.

VS Industry Bhd slipped one sen to 28.5 sen on 64.02 million shares traded, while GIIB Holdings Bhd tumbled five sen to 10.5 sen, with 62.45 million shares transacted.

YTL Power International Bhd shed 39 sen to RM4.40, with 57.23 million shares changing hands.

Despite the weaker market performance, trading activity increased, with total turnover rising to 3.06 billion shares worth RM2.56 billion compared to 2.9 billion shares valued at RM2.33 billion on Nov 11.
